ne7b8c913279.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dated items)
ne7b8c913279.s: The Kapalikas, the skull-bowl ascetics, were an offshoot of which Shaiva sect?
ne7b8c913279.x: The Kapalikas were an offshoot of the Pasupata sect (APPSC G2 2019), not of the Kalamukhas.

n21234cf4153.s: The main centre of Veerashaivism in Andhra was:
n21234cf4153.x: Srisailam was the main Veerashaiva centre in Andhra; Kolanupaka is listed among Jain centres.

n6c86dcfc4ea.s: Basaveshwara, founder of Veerashaivism, was a minister of:
n6c86dcfc4ea.x: Basaveshwara was a minister of Kalachuri Bijjala in Karnataka.

n68d25d293b2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Kakatiya architectural terms?
o: Floating bricks reduce the dead weight of the tower
Stellate plans give greater wall surface for sculpture
Kirtimukha means the 'face of glory' motif
n68d25d293b2.x: Monolithic carving is denoted by Ekasila; Kirtimukha is the 'face of glory' motif.

n079b03d27e7.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: A Lover's Guide to Warangal (translation) – Jayapa Senani
n079b03d27e7.x: The translation 'A Lover's Guide to Warangal' is by David Shulman and Velcheru Narayana Rao; Jayapa Senani wrote Nritta Ratnavali.

n8c6421aff33.s: Who built the Prasanna Keshava Temple at Hanamkonda?
n8c6421aff33.x: Vellanki Gangadhara, a Vaishnava minister of Rudradeva, built the Prasanna Keshava Temple at Hanamkonda.

n7b95d465e24.s: Kakatiya temple architecture shows the influence of the:
n7b95d465e24.x: Kakatiya style shows Western Chalukya (Kalyani) influence in carved pillars, star platforms and ceilings (APPSC G2 2025).

nf67ebf5baa1.s: The innermost defensive enclosure of Warangal Fort was called:
nf67ebf5baa1.x: Warangal had three concentric lines of defence; Puttakota was the innermost and Kalukota the outer stone fort.

n71e3a529ac5.s: The bracket figures on the outer walls of the Ramappa Temple are called:
n71e3a529ac5.x: The Ramappa Temple has madanika bracket figures on its outer walls, besides a star-shaped platform and painted ceilings.

nd1685146043.s: How many pillars does the Thousand Pillar Temple at Hanamkonda actually have?
nd1685146043.x: It has 369 pillars; its lathe-turned pillars only give the illusion of a thousand.

nap-history-36-24.s: Which of the following did NOT belong to the Kakatiya dynasty?
nap-history-36-24.x: Recharla Rudra was a Kakatiya general from the Recherla family, not a member of the dynasty.

n2cb23582027.s: Who built the Thousand Pillar Temple at Hanamkonda?
n2cb23582027.x: The Thousand Pillar Temple was built by Rudradeva; Recherla Rudra built the Ramappa Temple.

nddbc3eae89a.s: The Ramappa (Rudreshwara) Temple at Palampet is named after its:
nddbc3eae89a.x: The Palampet temple, associated with floating bricks, is named after its sculptor Ramappa; it was built by Recherla Rudra.

n9568df3b8aa.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about temple architecture in Andhradesa?
o: The Chalukya-Chola style joined Pallava planning to early Chalukya elements
Vijayanagara temple architecture drew mainly on Hoysala and Kalinga styles
The Chalukya-Chola style became the model for the Godavari region
Kakatiya architecture is transitional between early Chalukyan and Vijayanagara styles
n9568df3b8aa.x: The statement that Vijayanagara architecture drew mainly on Hoysala and Kalinga styles is wrong; the other three are correct.

n4a6a7949ce5.s: Which of the following pairs about the Thousand Pillar Temple at Hanamkonda is INCORRECTLY matched?
n4a6a7949ce5.x: The temple was dedicated to Shiva, Vishnu and Surya, not to Brahma.

n41ce7d2c32c.s: Which is the only temple in Andhra Pradesh with two flagpoles?
n41ce7d2c32c.x: Simhachalam, the temple of Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha, is the only AP temple with two flagpoles (APPSC 2002).

nfdfc649717d.s: Kakatiya temples represent which temple order?
nfdfc649717d.x: Kakatiya temples are Vesara, the stepped blend of Nagara and southern features.

nd57b4d6e911.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler is credited with building 108 temples?
nd57b4d6e911.x: Vijayaditya II is credited with building 108 temples; Chalukya Bhima I built Draksharama.

nc0833bd8a42.s: Who built the Veera Siromandapam at Srisailam?
nc0833bd8a42.x: Anavema Reddy built the Veera Siromandapam; Prolaya Vema's 1346 work was completing the steps to Patalaganga.

n3970880158c.s: The Draksharama temple, a model of the Chalukya-Chola style, was built by:
n3970880158c.x: Draksharama was built by Chalukya Bhima I and later renovated and endowed by the Reddis.

n44f60af227e.s: Kumararama, one of the Pancharamas, is located at:
n44f60af227e.x: Kumararama is at Samalkot (Chalukya Bhimavaram); Somarama is at Bhimavaram, Ksheerarama at Palakollu and Amararama at Amaravati.

n630a3dc4a5b.s: Which temple at Pattadakal is built in the Nagara form?
n630a3dc4a5b.x: At Pattadakal the Papanatha temple is Nagara, while the Virupaksha temple is Dravida.

nb519d530749.s: The Undavalli caves were excavated under which dynasty?
nb519d530749.x: The Undavalli caves (4th-5th c.) are Vishnukundina, cut top-down into a sandstone hill; the reclining Ananta Padmanabha is a Vishnukundina granite monolith.

n6a3e90c40e8.s: A temple with three shrines on one plan is called a:
n6a3e90c40e8.x: A trikutalaya has three shrines on one plan, e.g. the Thousand Pillar temple.

n65262429102.s: Kakatiya painting associated with ____ led on to the Lepakshi style.
n65262429102.x: Kakatiya painting associated with Machaladevi led on to the Lepakshi style.

n321b1566c90.s: Jayapa Senani, author of Nrittaratnavali, was a commander of:
n321b1566c90.x: Jayapa Senani was Ganapatideva's commander; his Nrittaratnavali covers both marga and desi dance.

n1817f4d4425.s: The Shakti peetha of Manikyamba is at:
n1817f4d4425.x: Manikyamba is associated with Draksharama, while Bhramaramba is associated with Srisailam.

nca84304aff3.x: Ramappa dates to 1213; the Thousand Pillar Temple is of 1163 and the Siddhavatam inscription of 1233.

na3403b590ee.s: Which fort replaced Addanki as the Reddi capital?
na3403b590ee.x: Kondaveedu replaced Addanki as the Reddi capital and later became a battleground between the Gajapatis and Vijayanagara.

n710a2e1aed5.s: In which year did Gajarao Tippa defeat Firoz Shah's army at Kambhammetta?
n710a2e1aed5.x: Gajarao Tippa defeated Firoz Shah's army at Kambhammetta in 1396; the Bahmani attack on Kandukur was repelled in 1398.

n534ebf3e4d6.s: Srinatha dedicated his Sringara Naishadham to:
n534ebf3e4d6.x: Sringara Naishadham, based on Sriharsha's Naishadhiyacharita, was dedicated to Mamidi Singana; Haravilasam went to Tippayya Setti.

n663d3c9f7b9.s: Which Rajamahendravaram figure was killed at Kakaraparthi in 1414 by Gajaraju Tippa?
n663d3c9f7b9.x: Kataya Vema was killed at Kakaraparthi (1414) by Gajaraju Tippa; Allada Reddi then ran the state as regent.

n4dd3d9b4f47.s: Kumaragiri Reddi was known by the title:
n4dd3d9b4f47.x: Karpura Vasantaraya was Kumaragiri's title; Veeranna Pothu belonged to Anavota, Andhra Suratrana to Anavema and Bharatamata Patanga to Sivalinga Reddi.

n7364d649ddb.s: In which year did Pedakomati Vema oust Kumaragiri Reddi?
n7364d649ddb.x: Pedakomati Vema ousted Kumaragiri in 1402, after which Kumaragiri fled to Rajahmundry.

n4601603396a.s: Which Gajapati ruler annexed Rajahmundry during 1446–48?
n4601603396a.x: After the death of Deva Raya II, Kapileswara Gajapati annexed Rajahmundry (1446–48).

n1f1457f07da.x: Dweepa Vijetha was Anavota Reddi's title; Prolaya Vema was Dharma Pratishtana Nagarudu.

n2e0d502ff52.s: At Vijayanagara, Srinatha defeated which court poet of Devaraya II?
n2e0d502ff52.x: Srinatha defeated Gauda Dindima Bhatta of Devaraya II's court and was honoured with Kanakabhishekam.

nf6cecf23be4.s: The Anavemagiri mandapas at Simhachalam were built by:
nf6cecf23be4.x: Anavema Reddi built the Anavemagiri mandapas at Simhachalam and the Veera Siromandapam at Srisailam.

n12f5e4771e4.s: Pedakomati Vema, who opposed Kumaragiri's accession, was pacified by being made the feudatory of:
n12f5e4771e4.x: Kumaragiri made Pedakomati Vema the feudatory of Chandolu and designated him heir.

na5d5edeff56.s: In 1404, Pedakomati Vema recovered lost territory from:
na5d5edeff56.x: Pedakomati Vema recovered lost land from Vijayanagara in 1404.

n609adb636df.s: The warrior-farmer backbone of Kakatiya–Reddi society, supplying most soldiers, was formed by:
n609adb636df.x: Kammas, Kapus, Reddis and Velamas formed the warrior-farmer backbone and supplied most of the soldiers.

nf7b34b67ef3.s: In Kakatiya usage, Pullari was a tax on:
nf7b34b67ef3.x: Pullari was the cattle-grazing tax; Illari was the house tax, Ari the land tax and Kanika the gifts.

n8c0cb63bb04.s: Annadeva captured parts of Vengi from Allada Reddi with the support of the:
n8c0cb63bb04.x: Annadeva captured parts of Vengi with Velama support, one of the challenges faced by Allada Reddi.

n53823713ba3.s: The Ghoderayas, whose disciples included the Reddi kings, propagated Shaivism from:
n53823713ba3.x: The Ghoderayas spread Shaivism from Tripurantakam; the Vadagalai matha was at Ahobilam.

ne7fb73ce66f.s: The poet Errana was associated with which Reddi ruler?
ne7fb73ce66f.x: Errana was associated with Prolaya Vema; Bala Saraswati with Anavota, and Srinatha and Vamana Bhatta Bana with Pedakomati Vema.

na217945e0b6.s: During the Reddi period, Devadasis trained in music, dance and ritual were respected performers at:
na217945e0b6.x: Devadasis were respected performers at Shiva temples, including the Pancharamas.

n6cec2f0d383.s: Kavyalankara Chudamani, linked to Rajahmundry as a literary hub, was written by:
n6cec2f0d383.x: Kavyalankara Chudamani is by Vinnakota Peddana; Sivalila Vilasamu is by Sivaleka Kommana and Kashikhandam by Srinatha.

n24078cf58f7.s: Which Reddi ruler abolished the tax on gold?
n24078cf58f7.x: Anavota abolished the gold tax; his minister Somaya issued the Abhaya Sasanam at Motupalli to encourage trade.

n5b873c20289.s: The crop share given to village Ayagars as remuneration was called:
n5b873c20289.x: Ayagars were paid in Manyam land or through a crop share called Mera.

nap-history-21-18.s: Kanaka Rekha Kalyanam was written by:
nap-history-21-18.x: Kanaka Rekha Kalyanam is by Vamana Bhanu Bhattu; Haravilasam, Srungara Naishadham and Palnati Veera Charitra are Srinatha's.

nacc0f9405fd.s: Kumaragiri Rajiyam, a commentary on Kalidasa's three plays, was written by:
nacc0f9405fd.x: Kumaragiri Rajiyam was written by Kataya Vema Reddi, Kumaragiri's brother-in-law, and only named after Kumaragiri.

nap-history-44-18.s: The title 'Rayagaja Kesari' was borne by:
nap-history-44-18.x: Rudramadevi bore the title Rayagaja Kesari; Kumaragiri Reddy was Karpura Vasanta Rayalu.

nap-history-18-5.s: The Pakala Tank, built in Ganapatideva's reign, was constructed by his general:
nap-history-18-5.x: The Pakala tank was built in Ganapatideva's reign by his general Jagadala Mummadi.

nap-history-36-4.s: Prolaya Vema Reddy founded the Reddy kingdom in:
nap-history-36-4.x: Prolaya Vema Reddy founded the Reddy kingdom in 1324.

nindian-history-1-90.s: The Motupalli epigraph is chiefly known for fixing:
nindian-history-1-90.x: The Motupalli epigraph fixes commodity tariffs and shows imports and exports; famine relief belongs to the Mahasthan inscription.

nap-history-18-14.s: Prolaya Vema Reddy built stepped pathways to Ahobilam and to the Pathala Ganga descent at:
nap-history-18-14.x: He built the Sopanamargas to ease pilgrimage to Ahobilam and the steep descent to Pathala Ganga at Srisailam.

nap-history-21-13.s: Saptha Sathi Saara Teeka was written by:
nap-history-21-13.x: Pedakomati Vema Reddy wrote Sahitya Chintamani and Saptha Sathi Saara Teeka.

nap-history-21-17.x: Bogini Dandakam is by Bammera Potana, a contemporary of Pedakomati Vema Reddy and Srinatha.

nap-history-2-5.s: Who was the last ruler of the Kondaveedu Reddy kingdom?
nap-history-2-5.x: Racha Vema Reddy was the last ruler of the Kondaveedu Reddy line.

nap-history-21-5.s: Who was the last poet of the Kavitrayam?
nap-history-21-5.x: Errana was the last poet of the Kavitrayam.

nap-history-44-11.x: Dharma Durgavibhala was Prolaya Vema Reddy's title; Pedakomati Vema Reddy was known as Sarvagna.

nap-history-3-19.s: According to the Mutnuri inscription, the steps to Pathala Ganga at Srisailam were completed in:
nap-history-3-19.x: The Mutnuri inscription records the steps being finished in 1346; Prolaya Vema Reddy ruled till 1353.

nap-history-21-14.x: Vamana Bhanu Bhattu wrote Usha Parinayam; Bammera Potana wrote Veera Bhadra Vijayam.

nf965e06feb9.s: Which of the following was NOT among Anavema Reddi's conquests from the Kalinga Gajapatis?
nf965e06feb9.x: Anavema took Nidadavolu, Rajahmundry, Pithapuram, Simhachalam and Konaseema; Kandukur is not among them.

n57f52d903ac.s:
Assertion (A): The battle of Bhimavaram (1367–68) marked the end of Musunuri rule.
Reason (R): Musunuri Kapaya was killed in that battle fighting Anapota Nayaka.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n57f52d903ac.x: Anapota Nayaka defeated Musunuri Kapaya at Bhimavaram in 1367–68; Kapaya's death ended Musunuri rule.

nap-history-31-20.s: The capital of Anupa under Gautamiputra Satakarni was:
nap-history-31-20.x: Mahishmathi was the capital of Anupa; Koduru was the Brihatpalayana capital and Penugonda the post-Tallikota Vijayanagara capital.

nc068a385a35.s: The Vilasa copper-plate grant of 1330 was issued by:
nc068a385a35.x: The Vilasa grant of Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka describes Tughluq atrocities and his restoration of agraharas; Anitalli issued the Kaluvacheru grant of 1423.

nc0cbb50efaf.s: Kapaya Nayaka received help from which Vijayanagara ruler?
nc0cbb50efaf.x: Kapaya received help from Bukka I of Vijayanagara and also sought help from Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

n5b2a9a8a4d9.s: The title Andhradesadhisvara, used by Kapaya Nayaka, had earlier been held by Kakatiya:
n5b2a9a8a4d9.x: Andhradesadhisvara had earlier been used by Kakatiya Ganapatideva.

n6acbabc424a.s: The Recherla Velama kingdom is generally dated to:
n6acbabc424a.x: The Recherla kingdom is dated c. 1325–1475, about 150 years; it began as loyal feudatories of the early Kakatiyas.

n838eeb10699.s: Prolaya Nayaka, Recherla Singama and Prolaya Vema Reddi survived the fall of Warangal as generals of:
n838eeb10699.x: These three were the surviving generals of Prataparudra after the fall of Warangal.

nap-history-31-18.s: Vengipuram was the capital of the:
nap-history-31-18.x: The Salankayanas ruled from Vengipuram; the Ikshvakus from Vijayapuri and the Satavahanas from Paithan.

n9c8119f20f2.s: Ferishta's Persian work Tarikh-i-Ferishta refers to Telangana as:
n9c8119f20f2.x: Tarikh-i-Ferishta calls Telangana 'Tilang' and describes the Bahmani-Kapaya conflicts.

nap-history-43-5.s: The capital of the Musunuri kingdom was:

n8f2f8d76d24.s: In which year did Kapaya Nayaka recover Warangal from Malik Maqbul?
n8f2f8d76d24.x: Warangal was recovered in 1336; the Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347 and Bhuvanagiri was lost in 1356.

nap-history-31-4.s: Anapota Reddy moved the Reddy capital from Addanki to:
nap-history-31-4.x: Prolaya Vema Reddi ruled from Addanki and Anapota Reddy moved the capital to Kondaveedu.

nc61241c8c7d.s: The Reddi successor state is approximately dated to:
nc61241c8c7d.x: The Reddi state is dated 1325–1448, while the Recherla Velama state is dated 1325–1475.

nec991674286.x: Kapaya recovered Warangal, while Singama cleared Nalgonda–Mahabubnagar and Prolaya Vema Reddi cleared Kammanadu–Pakanadu.

n6a1760bea1a.s: The successor states that arose after the loss of Kakatiya unity were the:
o: Musunuri, Recherla Velama and Reddi states
Kalyani Chalukya, Velama and Reddi states
n6a1760bea1a.x: The loss of Kakatiya unity gave rise to the Musunuri, Recherla Velama and Reddi successor states.

n8c116d69343.s: Under the truce of 1364–65 with the Bahmanis, Kapaya Nayaka ceded:
n8c116d69343.x: Kapaya ceded Golconda fort with huge wealth, and Golconda became the boundary between the two powers.

n3b93716c436.s: After its fall, Muhammad bin Tughlaq renamed Warangal as:
n3b93716c436.x: Warangal was renamed Sultanpurti and Andhra placed under Malik Burhanuddin, assisted by Malik Maqbul.

nf285c0fc764.s: Prataparudra Gajapati lost Udayagiri, Kondaveedu and Kondapalli to:
nf285c0fc764.x: Prataparudra Gajapati lost these forts to Krishnadevaraya (1513–1519).

n4f44606a05c.s: Under Gajapati rule in Andhra, revenue was collected and order maintained by local chiefs called:
n4f44606a05c.x: Nayakas and samantas collected revenue and maintained order; the Reddi-era social order was retained.

n955a267b58f.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dated items)
n955a267b58f.s: Hamvira, who defeated the Bahmani army attacking Devarakonda, was the son of:
n955a267b58f.x: Hamvira was the son of Kapileswara Gajapati and defeated the Bahmani army that attacked Devarakonda.

n423f0295e10.s: Firoz Shah's army was repulsed at Kandukuru in 1398 by:
n423f0295e10.x: Machareddi repulsed Firoz Shah at Kandukuru in 1398; Gajarao Tippa beat him at Kambhammetta in 1396.

n60984726262.x: Gajapati means 'Lord of Elephants'; the Gajapatis ruled from Cuttack.

n0ad2cf6a159.s: Kondaveedu, held by Vijayanagara until 1449, fell to the Gajapatis around:
n0ad2cf6a159.x: Kondaveedu was under Vijayanagara until 1449 and fell to the Gajapatis around 1450.

n13c6b125ccc.s: Krishnadevaraya's campaign against Prataparudra Gajapati began with the capture of:
n13c6b125ccc.x: The campaign went through Udayagiri, Kondaveedu, Kondapalli and Bejawada, then the march to Cuttack in 1518.

n2e36976a9be.s: Which Bahmani leader subdued Orugallu and took Kondaveedu?
n2e36976a9be.x: With Muhammad III, Mahmud Gawan suppressed Telangana revolts from 1453, subdued Orugallu and took Kondaveedu.

nd280a814143.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Prabandha form?
o: The epic kavya gave way to the prabandha
The prabandha dispenses with strict metrical rules
The prabandha generally treats a single episode
The prabandha has elaborate descriptions and strong shringara
nd280a814143.x: The prabandha follows strict metrical rules, so the statement that it dispenses with them is false.

n49fb426adf5.s: Which inscription contains the first Madhyakkara poem?
n49fb426adf5.x: Bezawada has the first Madhyakkara poem; Addanki is the first Telugu poetic inscription in Taruvoja metre.

n3f2de0f28aa.s: Sarala Dasa composed the Mahabharata in:
n3f2de0f28aa.x: Sarala Dasa composed the Mahabharata in Odia; Kasirama Das composed it in Bengali.

n567e532c156.s: The line 'Desa Bhashalandu Telugu Lessa' is associated with:
n567e532c156.x: The line is associated with Krishnadevaraya, whose period with the Ashtadiggajas was the peak of Telugu literary culture.

n22e7746c429.s: Kreedabhiramam is a Telugu rendering of Premabhiramam, a Sanskrit play by:
n22e7746c429.x: Kreedabhiramam renders Ravipati Tripurantakudu's Premabhiramam, hence the authorship debate with Vinukonda Vallabharaya.

n403d1ca8796.s: Who translated the Markandeya Puranam into Telugu?
n403d1ca8796.x: Marana translated Markandeya Puranam; Errana did Harivamsa and Ketana Dasakumara Charitra.

na66c28b5e78.x: Parijatapaharanam is by Nandi Timmana; Manucharitra is by Allasani Peddana.

n3ca16d30856.s: Palkuriki Somanatha, hailed as Prathama Andhra Viplava Kavi, led which literary movement?
n3ca16d30856.x: He led the Desi kavita movement against the Sanskritised marga style, popularising dwipada, ragada and other desi metres.

n123350ab8c2.s: Which courts supported Srinatha and Errana in the Prabandha tradition?
n123350ab8c2.x: The Reddi courts supported Srinatha and Errana, and the Vijayanagara Nayaka courts helped spread the style.

n8d87c4ee29d.s: Prataparudra Yashobhushanam, a Sanskrit work, was written by:
n8d87c4ee29d.x: Prataparudra Yashobhushanam is a Sanskrit work by Vidyanatha, not a Telugu work by Ketana.

n02e362dd654.x: Bhimakhandam concerns Bhimeswara of Draksharama; Sringara Naishadham is on Nala and Damayanti and Palnati Veera Charitra on the battle of Palnadu.

n0ba92d27268.s: Tikkana's first work, dedicated to Manumasiddhi, was:
n0ba92d27268.x: Nirvachanottara Ramayanam was Tikkana's first work, dedicated to Manumasiddhi; Basava Puranam is by Palkuriki Somanatha.

n7c6bb400422.s: The Gatha Saptasati, a Prakrit work containing early Telugu words, was compiled by:
n7c6bb400422.x: The Satavahana king Hala compiled the Gatha Saptasati, which holds words like atta, addam, potta and pilla.

n4183fa6a7bb.s: Nannaya borrowed the Akkara metre from:
n4183fa6a7bb.x: The Akkara metre was borrowed from Kannada, not Tamil; Nannaya also pioneered the Champu style.

n7478804e8f5.s: Who is identified as the first prabandha writer in Telugu?
n7478804e8f5.x: Errana is identified as the first prabandha writer; Nannechoda began the tradition of the eight descriptions.

n3e4daffa033.s: Telugu, the official language of Andhra Pradesh, belongs to which language family?
n3e4daffa033.x: Telugu belongs to the Dravidian family and is one of the 22 Eighth Schedule languages.

nf3778b1c053.s: Srinatha wrote Kashikhandam at the request of:
nf3778b1c053.x: Kashikhandam was written at Kataya Vema's request; Haravilasam was dedicated to Tippayya Setti.

nc00a9b19c9e.s: Narayana Bhattu, who knew eight languages, bore the title:
nc00a9b19c9e.x: Narayana Bhattu was Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara and represented Someshwara I of Kalyani at Rajamahendravaram.

na00a9c40a56.s: The first Telugu grammar, written in Sanskrit, is:
na00a9c40a56.x: Andhra Shabda Chintamani is the first Telugu grammar in Sanskrit; Ganita Sara Sangraha is the first Telugu mathematics book.

nd1973acc230.s: In Eastern Chalukya inscriptions, the official language was:
nd1973acc230.x: Sanskrit was official while Telugu was the people's language; in bilingual records the eulogy was in Sanskrit and grant details in Telugu.

n37a9dbda156.s: Which of the following is NOT among the inscriptions showing written Telugu before Nannaya?
n37a9dbda156.x: Kalamalla, Vipparla, Addanki and Bezawada show pre-Nannaya written Telugu; the Motupalli epigraph is a later Kakatiya-era record.

n650fd7de4cd.s: The Kesari Samudra tank was built by Kakatiya:
n650fd7de4cd.x: Rudradeva, author of Nitisara, is associated with building the Kesari Samudra tank.

n24bcdf3cc77.s: Ketana earned the title 'Abhinava Dandi' for rendering into Telugu:
n24bcdf3cc77.x: His Dashakumara Charitra, from Dandin's Sanskrit work, is the first Telugu prose-story kavya and won him the title (APPSC G2 2019).

n22840772289.s: Tikkana was the court poet of:
n22840772289.x: Tikkana served Manumasiddhi II of Nellore; Errana was at Prolaya Vema Reddi's court and Rajaraja Narendra patronised Nannaya.

nf4a552bb0b3.s: Ketana, known as Mula Ghatika, dedicated his work to:
nf4a552bb0b3.x: Ketana dedicated his work to Tikkana and was the first to use the words 'Tenugu' and 'Telugu'.

n948d7addd44.s: The epithet 'Italian of the East' for Telugu was coined by:
n948d7addd44.x: It was coined by the 15th-century Venetian traveller Niccolo de' Conti; 'Desa bhashalandu Telugu lessa' is Krishnadevaraya's.

n6b2304de83a.s: Which of the following was a member of the Kavitraya?
n6b2304de83a.x: The Kavitraya consists of Nannaya, Tikkana and Errana.

n1e795fb41de.x: Vrushadhipa Satakam is by Palkuriki Somanatha; Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya wrote Sivatattvasaram.

nc939ce577ff.s: Palkuriki Somanatha's Basava Puranam was composed in which metre?
nc939ce577ff.x: Basava Puranam is in the native dwipada metre, which Somanatha popularised, not in Champu style.

n49275e9dc18.x: Ubhayakavimitrudu is Tikkana's title; Nannaya was Vaganusasana and Errana Sambhudasa.

n159717ad691.s: The Sanskrit work Varadambika Parinayam was written by:
n159717ad691.x: Varadambika Parinayam is by Tirumalamba (APPSC G2 2017); Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam.

ne050f4221c6.s: Tikkana, who dedicated his work to Hariharanatha, preached:
ne050f4221c6.x: Tikkana preached Harihara Advaita, the unity of Shiva and Vishnu; Ketana was his disciple.

nde838d31b45.s: Telugu belongs to which sub-branch of the Dravidian family?
nde838d31b45.x: Telugu is South-Central Dravidian with Gondi and Kui; Tamil and Malayalam are South Dravidian.

n6debf23fcc3.s: How many parvas of the Mahabharata did Tikkana translate into Telugu?
n6debf23fcc3.x: Tikkana translated the remaining 15 parvas, from Virata to Swargarohana, and called it Prabandha Mandali.

n3951339ab54.s: The separate Telugu script with rounded letters and vowel signs emerged in the:
n3951339ab54.x: After the Bhattiprolu Brahmi variant and the common Old Kannada–Telugu script, the separate Telugu script came in the 11th–14th centuries.

n517f488189e.s: Errana completed which parva of the Mahabharata left unfinished by Nannaya?
n517f488189e.x: By completing the Aranya Parva, Errana linked Nannaya's work with Tikkana's.

nindian-history-46-38.x: Baihaqi wrote Tarikh-i-Subuktigin; Utbi wrote Kitab-ul-Yamini and Al-Biruni Kitab-ul-Hind.

n95fe8db2c01.s: Which of the following did NOT confine Arab rule to Sindh?
o: The strength of the Pratiharas, Rashtrakutas and Palas
Complete political unity in North India
n95fe8db2c01.x: North India was not completely united; geography, strong regional states and weak resources restricted the Arabs.

nindian-history-21-10.s: Mahmud Ghazni raided the Chakraswamin temple at Thanesar in:
nindian-history-21-10.x: Thanesar was raided in 1014; Mathura was sacked in 1018 and Somnath raided in 1025–26.

nindian-history-45-16.s: Who was the poet laureate (Malik-ush-Shuara) of Mahmud Ghaznavi's court?
nindian-history-45-16.x: Unsuri was poet laureate; Firdausi wrote the Shahnama and Utbi Kitab-ul-Yamini.

nbfe23766428.s: The First Battle of Tarain (1191) arose over:
nbfe23766428.x: Tabarhinda (Bhatinda) was the cause; Prithviraj Chauhan won and Ghori barely escaped.

n2708ba8df4b.s: The Second Battle of Tarain was fought in:
n2708ba8df4b.x: The Second Battle of Tarain was fought in 1192, the First in 1191, both against Prithviraj Chauhan.

n5179093be3f.s: The capital of Raja Dahir, defeated by Muhammad bin Qasim in 712 CE, was:
n5179093be3f.x: Dahir's capital was Alor (Aror); Brahmanabad was only one of the places taken.

n85ec40bc8ad.s: Al-Biruni's Kitab-ul-Hind is an objective account of India in the:
n85ec40bc8ad.x: Al-Biruni's Kitab-ul-Hind is an objective account of eleventh-century India.

nindian-history-20-9.s: Who entered Nadiya, drove Lakshman Sen to East Bengal and captured Lakhnauti?
nindian-history-20-9.x: Bakhtiyar Khalji conquered Bengal for the Ghurids after taking Bihar and destroying Nalanda and Vikramshila.

neca005d99c5.s: The fragmentation of Rajput states that aided the Turks followed the collapse of the:
neca005d99c5.x: After the Pratiharas collapsed, Rajput states fragmented and competed, and this disunity helped the Turks.

nindian-history-19-8.s: Muhammad Ghori defeated Jayachandra (Jaichand) of Kannauj at the Battle of:
nindian-history-19-8.x: Ghori defeated Jayachandra at Chandawar (1194), near the Yamuna.

nindian-history-21-9.s: How many times did Mahmud of Ghazni invade India between 1000 and 1027?
nindian-history-21-9.x: Mahmud raided India 17 times between 1000 and 1027.

nindian-history-6-3.s: Al-Biruni's Arabic translation of Patanjali's Yoga-Sutra is titled:
nindian-history-6-3.x: Al-Biruni translated the Yoga-Sutra into Arabic as Kitab Patanjal.

n89f252bc822.s: Unlike Mahmud of Ghazni, who mainly raided for plunder, Muhammad Ghori aimed at:
n89f252bc822.x: Mahmud was mainly a plunder-seeking raider, while Ghori pursued conquest and a lasting political presence in North India.

na7b3daecb55.s: Which of the following is NOT among the features of Indian feudalism that R. S. Sharma linked to Turkish success?
o: Universal military participation across all castes
na7b3daecb55.x: Sharma linked feudal levies, sub-infeudation and a closed village economy; caste restricted fighting to a few groups.

n698130b455c.s: The Maru-Gurjara style of the 11th–13th centuries is associated with the:
n698130b455c.x: Maru-Gurjara is a Solanki-associated Nagara sub-style of Gujarat and Rajasthan, fusing Maha-Maru and Maha-Gurjara traditions.

n26ec924c65a.s: Kumarapala encouraged Jainism under the influence of:
n26ec924c65a.x: Kumarapala encouraged Jainism under Hemachandra's influence; he also rebuilt Somnath and curbed animal slaughter.

ne1c02876abd.s: In R. S. Sharma's model of 'Indian feudalism', vishti means:
ne1c02876abd.x: Sharma's model includes sub-infeudation and vishti (forced labour), with closed village economies.

n737ab878f56.s: Khajuraho and Mahoba in Bundelkhand are associated with the:
n737ab878f56.x: The Chandelas held Bundelkhand with Khajuraho and Mahoba; the Paramaras held Malwa and the Gahadavalas Kanauj and Varanasi.

nc7a8f256231.s: Bhojshala at Dhar, linked to Paramara Bhoja, is called by Muslims the:
nc7a8f256231.x: Muslims call Bhojshala the Kamal Maula Mosque; it became a mosque in the 14th century.

na2ca11f2606.s: The Modhera Sun temple was built by the Solanki ruler:
na2ca11f2606.x: Bhima I built the Modhera Sun temple; Somnath was sacked in 1025 during his reign.

n7bb21166518.s: Rani-ki-Vav at Patan was built by Udayamati in memory of:
n7bb21166518.x: Rani-ki-Vav was built by Udayamati, queen of Bhima I, in his memory.

n458056e7e5c.s: The Tomaras, whose coins carried a horseman-and-bull motif, ruled from:
n458056e7e5c.x: The Tomaras held Dhillika (Delhi); the Mehrauli Iron Pillar is a Gupta work only moved there.

n1316c54bd54.s: Alha Khand, linked with the Chandela Paramardi, was written by:
n1316c54bd54.x: Alha Khand is by Jagnik; Chand Bardai wrote Prithviraj Raso and Narapati Nalha Bisaldeva Raso.

nc8f63a4c294.s: Which inscription gives the Paramara genealogy and praises Bhoja?
nc8f63a4c294.x: The Udaipur Prashasti gives the Paramara genealogy and praises Bhoja.

n641c16c2797.s: The Kandariya Mahadeva temple at Khajuraho is dedicated to:
n641c16c2797.x: Kandariya Mahadeva (by Vidyadhara) is a Shiva temple; the Lakshmana temple is Vishnu's.

n625992a5a00.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the traditional four Agnikula Rajput clans?
n625992a5a00.x: The four Agnikula clans are Paramara, Pratihara, Chauhan and Solanki; the Chandelas are off the traditional list.

n2af25e6fdc0.x: Navasahasanka Charita is by Padmagupta; Bhoja wrote Samarangana Sutradhara and Dalpati Vijay Khuman Raso.

nap-history-23-2.s: Marco Polo visited Andhra during the reign of:
nap-history-23-2.x: Marco Polo came in Rudramadevi's reign; Nicolo Conti came under Devaraya I.

n33f9137f552.s: In Qutb Shahi calligraphy, Quranic verses were written in the script:
n33f9137f552.x: Naskh was used for Quranic verses, including those in the Jami Masjid mihrab; Nastaliq was used for Persian texts.

n4312ca8c04d.x: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was dedicated to Nasiruddin Mahmud; Hasan Nizami's Taj-ul-Maasir was patronised by Aibak.

n48b498ae34d.x: Firishta, born at Astarabad in 1552, dedicated his work to Ibrahim Adil Shah of Bijapur, not to a Qutb Shahi ruler.

nindian-history-6-17.x: Tabqat-i-Nasiri is by Minhaj-us-Siraj; Khazain-ul-Futuh is by Amir Khusrau.

nindian-history-6-4.x: Fawaid-ul-Fawad is by Amir Hasan Sijzi; Barani wrote Fatwa-i-Jahandari and Hasan Nizami Taj-ul-Masir.

nap-history-23-4.s: Tavernier, the 17th-century traveller, visited Andhra to see its:
nap-history-23-4.x: Tavernier, a 17th-century French jeweller, visited the Golconda-Andhra diamond mines for trade.

ndfd20709b62.s: According to Telugu sources such as Pratapa Charitra, how many times was Warangal invaded?
ndfd20709b62.x: Telugu sources (Pratapa Charitra, Vilasa, Kaluvacheru) record eight invasions; Muslim sources record five.

nap-history-23-15.s: Itsing, who saw Indian students memorising Nagarjuna's Suhrllekha, was a pilgrim from:

necbfc12b3e6.s: Which traveller is associated with Motupalli?
necbfc12b3e6.x: Marco Polo is associated with Motupalli; Abdur Razzaq and Barbosa with Vijayanagara, and Tavernier with Golconda.

n006ebfd9b15.s: Firishta's story that Deva Raya kidnapped Nehal is, by modern historians:
n006ebfd9b15.x: Modern historians reject Firishta's story that Deva Raya kidnapped Nehal, showing the need to evaluate chronicles critically.

n2734b15d75c.s: Who wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh and accompanied Malik Kafur's 1310 invasion of Warangal?
n2734b15d75c.x: Amir Khusrau, court poet of Alauddin Khalji, wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh and accompanied the 1310 expedition.

nf5d7dba98de.s: Al-Biruni, who learned Sanskrit, wrote his account of India in:
nf5d7dba98de.x: Al-Biruni learned Sanskrit and wrote in Arabic on Indian religion, philosophy, astronomy and caste.

nec1231c4dd8.s: The Palam Baoli inscription of 1276, a Sanskrit record, praises:
nec1231c4dd8.x: The Palam Baoli inscription praises Balban; the Vilasa copper plate belongs to Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka.

n67a257f9140.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Iltutmish is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Mansur (1229) – Investiture from the Abbasid Caliph
Iqta – Revenue assignment in place of cash salary
Turkan-i-Chahalgani – Body of Persian revenue clerks
n67a257f9140.x: The Turkan-i-Chahalgani (the Forty) was the Turkish military elite, not a body of Persian revenue clerks.

n30cafa5509b.s: Balban broke the power of the Forty by:
n30cafa5509b.x: Balban broke the Forty's power by promoting junior Turks; he did not strengthen the Forty.

nc2799185918.x: Balban held the Sultan to be Zil-i-Ilahi (shadow of God) and required sijda and paibos.

nf05db95fe21.x: Lakh Bakhsh means 'giver of lakhs'; 'shadow of God' (Zil-i-Ilahi) is Balban's idea of the Sultan.

n1edf9bb9eef.s: Iltutmish shifted the capital of the Sultanate from:
n1edf9bb9eef.x: Iltutmish moved the capital from Lahore (Aibak's capital) to Delhi.

n3b16cffa947.s: Which Mamluk ruler immediately preceded Balban?
n3b16cffa947.x: Nasiruddin Mahmud (1246-66) was followed by Balban (1266-86).

n6acd7de6bbe.s: The Qutb Minar, begun by Qutbuddin Aibak, was completed by:
n6acd7de6bbe.x: Aibak began the Qutb Minar, but it was completed by Iltutmish.

nd339289d907.s: Iltutmish refused shelter to which Khwarazmian prince, helping keep Chengiz Khan out of India?
nd339289d907.x: Iltutmish refused shelter to Jalaluddin Mangbarni of Khwarazm, which helped keep Chengiz Khan out of India.

ndbb7e26dc13.s: Which of the following pairs on Kakatiya–Delhi relations is correctly matched?
o: 1309–10 – Kakatiya help to Delhi against the Pandyas
1311 – Treaty between Malik Kafur and the Kakatiyas
1303 – Kakatiya defeat of a Delhi army at Upparapalli
1316 – Start of Kakatiya tribute to Delhi
ndbb7e26dc13.x: The Kakatiyas defeated a Delhi army at Upparapalli in 1303; the treaty was 1309–10, help against the Pandyas 1311, and tribute stopped after 1316.

nf4c8c26974b.s: Mongols who converted and settled in the Sultanate under Jalaluddin Khalji were called:
nf4c8c26974b.x: Settled converted Mongols were called New Mussalmans; Jalaluddin also married his daughter to Ulugh Khan, a descendant of Chengiz Khan.

n9c236e181c6.x: Sikandar-i-Sani means the second Alexander; Alauddin wished to be a world conqueror like Alexander.

n317d01f50e1.s: Which Vaghela ruler of Gujarat was defeated by Alauddin Khalji's forces?
n317d01f50e1.x: Gujarat's Rai Karan (Karnadeva II Vaghela) was defeated; Ratan Singh was of Chittor and Mahlak Deva of Malwa.

n98ca3999cf7.s: Ghazi Malik's victory over ____ marked the end of Khalji rule.
n98ca3999cf7.x: Ghazi Malik's victory over Khusrau Khan ended Khalji rule.

n302711ccdf4.s: When the Mongols besieged Delhi, Alauddin Khalji took shelter in:
n302711ccdf4.x: Alauddin sheltered in Siri during the siege; Zafar Khan was killed at Kili.

n1e7d8eccf1e.s: The Padmini story, linked with Alauddin Khalji's conquest of Chittor, was recorded in Padmavat in:
n1e7d8eccf1e.x: The Padmini narrative was recorded in Padmavat in 1540; some scholars treat it as legend.

n8756a2d7b3e.s: Jalaluddin Khalji was murdered by Alauddin at:
n8756a2d7b3e.x: Jalaluddin, who crowned himself at Kilokhari, was murdered at Kara by Alauddin in 1296.

n91019d77f34.s: Malik Kafur's first southern campaign (1307-08) was against:
n91019d77f34.x: The order was Devagiri (1307-08), Warangal (1309-10), Dwarasamudra (1310-11) and Madurai (1311).

n8ad6802e8b8.s: Under Jalaluddin Khalji, Alauddin was Amir-i-Tuzuk, which means:
n8ad6802e8b8.x: Amir-i-Tuzuk was the master of ceremonies; the Ariz-i-Mumalik was the army minister.

nindian-history-21-16.s: Repeated Mongol invasions during Alauddin Khalji's reign led him to maintain:
o: a feudal levy of Rajput chiefs
nindian-history-21-16.x: The Mongol threat led Alauddin to keep a large standing army, with military reforms and revenue and market reforms to pay for it.

nindian-history-67-10.s: Genghis Khan reached the Indus around 1221 during the reign of:
nindian-history-67-10.x: Genghis Khan reached the Indus under Iltutmish; the 1398 invasion was by Timur.

nbe37d506f9b.s: Under Alauddin Khalji's southern policy, conquered rulers were generally:
o: allowed to keep their thrones on paying tribute
annexed and their kingdoms made provinces
nbe37d506f9b.x: In the south rulers kept their thrones and paid tribute, whereas northern kingdoms were generally annexed.

n41734c47546.s: Under Alauddin Khalji, the Sarai Adl market dealt in:
o: cloth, sugar, dry fruits, butter and oil
n41734c47546.x: Sarai Adl dealt in cloth and similar commodities; the Mandi handled food grains.

n5918c2e32db.s: Malik Kafur's second expedition against Warangal (1309–10) was accompanied by:
n5918c2e32db.x: Malik Kafur and Khwaja Haji besieged Warangal, won Prataparudra's submission and sent loot to Delhi on 1,000 camels.

n150a9a2426c.s: The headman's cess abolished by Alauddin Khalji was called:
n150a9a2426c.x: Alauddin abolished the kismat-i-khuti and brought khuts, muqaddams and chaudharis under taxation.

nafe95f9d5da.s: Barani's causes of revolt perceived by Alauddin were noble wealth, noble marriages and gatherings, drinking and:
nafe95f9d5da.x: Barani's four causes were noble wealth, noble intermarriage and gatherings, a weak intelligence system and drinking.

ncce1360aa51.s: Under Alauddin Khalji, the superintendent of an individual market was the:
ncce1360aa51.x: The Shahna-i-Mandi supervised each market; the system ran under the Diwan-i-Riyasat, who worked under the Naib-i-Riyasat.

nc5d5709c5e8.s: Alauddin Khalji fixed the state's share of produce (kharaj) at:
nc5d5709c5e8.x: The state share was one-half (50%); he was also the first Sultan to measure land, using the biswa.

n1f9ea6a903e.s: The main source for Alauddin Khalji's market control measures is:
n1f9ea6a903e.x: Barani is the main source; Mubarak Shah later abolished the controls.

nindian-history-23-7.s: Under Alauddin Khalji, Ghari was a tax on:
nindian-history-23-7.x: Ghari was the house tax; Charai was the grazing tax and Kharaj 50% of yield.

n817a8fa63c5.s: Amir Khusrau's Khazain-ul-Futuh describes the Warangal fort as:
o: a single mud wall with no moat
n817a8fa63c5.x: Khazain-ul-Futuh describes Warangal's double-walled fort, its moat and the diamond mines; Khusrau accompanied the 1310 campaign.

n27447158f87.s: Unlike Balban, Alauddin Khalji did not depend on ____ to justify his policies.
n27447158f87.x: Alauddin revived Balban's harsh, centralised rule but, unlike Balban, did not depend on religious sanction.

n443599ebd2f.s: Token currency, transfer of capital and canals are associated with the:
n443599ebd2f.x: The Tughlaqs are known for token currency, capital transfer and canals; the Khaljis for market control and the Lodis as the first Afghan dynasty.

n7ba22793dc2.s: Alauddin Khalji's market regulations aimed at price fixation, guaranteed supply, controlled distribution and:
n7ba22793dc2.x: The regulations fixed prices, guaranteed supply, controlled distribution and ended monopolistic practices.

nfbc033477ae.s: In matters of state policy, Alauddin Khalji declared that he would be guided by:
nfbc033477ae.x: Alauddin refused the Ulema's guidance and declared his actions would be governed by the interests of the state.

n7e827f452bb.s: Which of the following was NOT one of Alauddin Khalji's ordinances?
o: Confiscation of religious grants and free lands
Permission for nobles to form unrestricted marriage alliances
n7e827f452bb.x: Noble marriages and gatherings required royal permission; the other three were part of his ordinances.

nf7b4b3b31de.s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq made the iqtas:
nf7b4b3b31de.x: Firoz made iqtas hereditary; he also wrote off taqavi loans, fixed land revenue and kept the four Islamic taxes.

n4f095f79f59.s: Ghazi Malik became Sultan Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq in 1320 after killing:
n4f095f79f59.x: Ghazi Malik, earlier governor of Punjab, killed Khusrau Shah and became Sultan in 1320.

n8ffa67950fc.s: Muhammad bin Tughlaq's Qarachil (Kumaon hills) expedition aimed at:
n8ffa67950fc.x: The Qarachil expedition aimed to secure the hill frontier; the Khurasan expedition aimed at Central Asian conquest.

n213bde8f2db.s: The Madurai Sultanate was established in:
n213bde8f2db.x: The Madurai Sultanate dates to 1335, Vijayanagara to 1336 and the Bahmani kingdom to 1347.

n5a99810398c.s: Muhammad bin Tughlaq's higher taxation of the Doab, coinciding with a famine, led to:
n5a99810398c.x: Meant to raise revenue, the Doab tax increase coincided with famine and caused peasant revolts and flight.

nee15df5483d.s: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq died in 1325 when a wooden pavilion collapsed at:
nee15df5483d.x: He died at Afghanpur in 1325 (Ibn Battuta suspected Juna Khan); he had built Tughlaqabad.

n4074b6e01cf.s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq's irrigation cess, haq-i-sharb, was:
n4074b6e01cf.x: Haq-i-sharb was one-tenth; his canals carried water from the Yamuna and Sutlej to Hisar.

nindian-history-23-2-8.s: Under Firuz Tughlaq, about 1,300 Sanskrit manuscripts were obtained from the temple library of:
nindian-history-23-2-8.x: The manuscripts came from the Jawalamukhi temple library at Nagarkot, and Azizuddin Khalid Khani translated some into Persian.

nindian-history-97-7.s: The Dahsala system is associated with:
nindian-history-97-7.x: Todar Mal devised the Dahsala; Abul Fazl wrote Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari.

n7084ad7edb4.s: The Reddis expelled the Tughlaq forces from coastal Andhra around:
n7084ad7edb4.x: Coastal Andhra was freed around 1325, before the Madurai Sultanate (1335), Vijayanagara (1336) and the Bahmani kingdom (1347).

n6a3890d3621.s: Muhammad bin Tughlaq transferred his capital to Devagiri in:
n6a3890d3621.x: The capital was transferred in 1327; token currency followed around 1329–30.

n00c1c84c2fe.s: The first Sultan of Delhi to dig canals was:
n00c1c84c2fe.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq first dug canals; Firoz Shah dug the largest number.

n91e7e4991bd.s: Harihara and Bukka founded Vijayanagara under the guidance of:
n91e7e4991bd.x: Harihara and Bukka, sent by Muhammad bin Tughlaq, founded Vijayanagara under Vidyaranya's guidance.

n97fc38832f0.s: In 1342 Muhammad bin Tughlaq sent Ibn Battuta, the Qazi of Delhi, as envoy to:
n97fc38832f0.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq made Ibn Battuta Qazi of Delhi and sent him as envoy to China in 1342.

n4ea57ec434e.s: According to Ibn Battuta, horse couriers (uluq) were posted at intervals of:
n4ea57ec434e.x: Horse couriers were every four miles; foot couriers (dawa) had three stations to every mile.

n5d20f5e2bbb.s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq's two failed expeditions to Bengal were against:
n5d20f5e2bbb.x: Both Bengal campaigns against Haji Iliyas failed; Jam Babaniya of Sind agreed to pay tribute.

n0b526f6a169.s: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq limited any increase in land revenue to about:
n0b526f6a169.x: Ghiyasuddin limited any increase to about one-tenth and raised it gradually, besides drought remission and cultivation of waste land.

nindian-history-21-17.s: Babur defeated Medini Rai in 1528 at the Battle of:
nindian-history-21-17.x: Medini Rai was defeated at Chanderi (1528); Rana Sanga at Khanwa (1527) and the Afghans at Ghaghra (1529).

n14f15594a77.s: At Khatauli (1517-18), Ibrahim Lodi was defeated by:
n14f15594a77.x: At Khatauli Ibrahim was defeated by Rana Sanga; earlier he had made Vikramajit of Gwalior a vassal.

n1802ca6d087.s: The Gaz-i-Sikandari, a yard used to measure land, is associated with:
n1802ca6d087.x: Gaz-i-Sikandari was Sikandar Lodi's land-measuring yard; he also abolished several taxes and used audits and spies.

n0c4d256e0c5.s: At the First Battle of Panipat, Babur's flanking manoeuvre was called:
n0c4d256e0c5.x: Tulughma was the flanking manoeuvre; Araba carts chained together formed the defensive line.

n668f811e330.s: The first Afghan dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate was the:
n668f811e330.x: The Lodis were the first Afghan and the last dynasty of the Sultanate; Ibrahim Lodi was the last Delhi Sultan.

n790751f3cb3.s: Khizr Khan, Timur's viceroy, captured Delhi in:
n790751f3cb3.x: Khizr Khan arrested Daulat Khan Lodi and took Delhi in 1414, ruling as Timur's deputy without the title Sultan.

nef75c914267.s: Bahlol Lodi received the throne of Delhi from:
nef75c914267.x: Bahlol received the throne from Alam Shah, the last Sayyid; Khizr Khan founded the Sayyids.

nindian-history-19-6.s: The Battle of Khanwa was fought in:
nindian-history-19-6.x: First Panipat was 1526, Khanwa 1527, Chanderi 1528 and Ghaghra 1529.

n60ab8f8b6d3.s: Which of the following was NOT an effect of Timur's invasion of India?
o: Immediate establishment of the Mughal Empire in Delhi
Break-up of the Tughlaq state into regional kingdoms
Later rise of Khizr Khan's Sayyid dynasty
n60ab8f8b6d3.x: The Mughal Empire was established much later, by Babur in 1526.

nindian-history-82-11.s: The tanka and jital coins were issued by:
nindian-history-82-11.x: Iltutmish consolidated the Sultanate, issued the tanka and jital and completed the Qutub Minar.

n6ed6a5e9873.s: Iltutmish defeated Tajuddin Yalduz of Ghazni in 1215–16 at:
n6ed6a5e9873.x: Yalduz was defeated at Tarain in 1215–16; Qabacha of Multan and Sindh was suppressed in 1228.

nd6d4fd11d17.s: Rajon ki Baoli at Mehrauli, built in 1506, belongs to the reign of:
nd6d4fd11d17.x: 1506 falls in Sikandar Lodi's reign (1489-1517), not Ibrahim's.

na4b4d840028.s: The settlement founded by Harihara and Bukka that grew into Vijayanagara was:
na4b4d840028.x: Harihara and Bukka returned to Hinduism under Vidyaranya and founded Anegondi, which developed into Vijayanagara.

n2dc7e717d42.s: The Sayyid dynasty ruled the Delhi Sultanate during:
n2dc7e717d42.x: The Sayyids ruled 1414–1451; the Tughlaqs 1320–1414 and the Khaljis 1290–1320.

n41109873748.s: Ulugh Khan captured Prataparudra II, ending the Kakatiya kingdom, in:
n41109873748.x: Delhi invaded Andhra five times in 1303–1323; in 1323 Ulugh Khan captured Prataparudra II and the kingdom was annexed.

n67ef54cc840.s: The Battle of Khatoli was fought in:
n67ef54cc840.x: Khatoli was fought in 1517; Second Tarain was 1192 and Chandawar 1194.

nb82dd92e24e.s: The Mamluk dynasty was founded by:
nb82dd92e24e.x: Qutbuddin Aibak founded the Mamluk dynasty, not Iltutmish.

nindian-history-82-25.s: The founding of Agra is associated with:
nindian-history-82-25.x: The founding of Agra belongs to Sikandar Lodi; token currency and the move to Daulatabad belong to Muhammad bin Tughluq.

nindian-history-11-12.x: Iltutmish used Sultan and Sultan-i-Azam; Balban called himself Zil-i-Ilahi, the Shadow of God.

nindian-history-11-4.s: Qutbuddin Aybak was called 'Quran Khwan' because he:
nindian-history-11-4.x: Aybak was called Quran Khwan for his melodious Quran recitation; he ruled as Malik and never took the title Sultan.

n236df28cc4f.s: Which Khalji ruler was the child set up on the throne by Malik Kafur?
n236df28cc4f.x: After Alauddin, Malik Kafur set up the child Shihabuddin, who was followed by Mubarak Shah.

naf0aeece3bc.s: Which of the following pairs on Sultanate kingship is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Balban – Low-born men appointed to high offices
Alauddin Khalji – State interest placed above the ulema
Muhammad bin Tughlaq – Appointment of non-Turks and low-born men
naf0aeece3bc.x: Balban excluded low-born men from high office; appointing them is associated with Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

n3f48e60f918.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dated items)
n3f48e60f918.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, the Barid-i-Mumalik headed the:
n3f48e60f918.x: The Barid-i-Mumalik headed intelligence; the Qazi-ul-Quzat was Chief Justice and the Wakil-i-Dar ran the court and royal household.

n44dc1a5dd3a.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, the village headman was the:
n44dc1a5dd3a.x: The Muqaddam or Chaudhari was the village headman; Alauddin abolished the khut's cess.

n7239035f28c.x: Nizam-ul-Mulk Junaidi served Iltutmish, not Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

n1525af4a34e.s: Which of the following was NOT introduced by Balban to enhance the dignity of the Sultan?
n1525af4a34e.x: Balban introduced sijda, paibos and Nauroz; the Turkan-i-Chahalgani was created by Iltutmish.

nc5e0b185b35.s: The decimal organisation of the Sultanate army with mounted archers was a ____ element.
nc5e0b185b35.x: Decimal units and mounted archery were Turko-Mongol; the title Sultan and sijda, paibos and Nauroz were Perso-Arabic.

nc2a3dd11d9b.s: Royal correspondence and the drafting of decrees in the Delhi Sultanate were handled by the:
nc2a3dd11d9b.x: Diwan-i-Insha handled correspondence and decrees; Diwan-i-Wizarat dealt with finance and Diwan-i-Qaza with justice.

ndfeb619c0bc.s: Who destroyed the political influence of the Turkan-i-Chahalgani (the Forty)?
ndfeb619c0bc.x: Iltutmish created the Forty of Turkish slave-nobles; Balban destroyed their power.

nf0411629698.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, succession to the throne rested on:
o: acceptance by nobles and ulema, or military strength
nf0411629698.x: There was no fixed rule of succession; it rested on acceptance by nobles and ulema or on military strength.

n5ebb6383b9f.s: The wizarat of the Delhi Sultanate reached its heyday under:
n5ebb6383b9f.x: The wizarat's heyday was under Firoz Tughlaq, when Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul ran the government.

nindian-history-1-20.s: Whose coins showed Goddess Lakshmi on one side and the Kalma in Arabic on the other?
nindian-history-1-20.x: Muhammad Ghori's coins showed Lakshmi with the Kalma; Mahmud's silver coins used Arabic and Devanagari Sanskrit.

n90a3c4c19cf.s: Muhammad bin Tughlaq sought investiture from the Abbasid Caliph in:
n90a3c4c19cf.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq sought investiture from the Abbasid Caliph in Egypt; Iltutmish received the Baghdad investiture in 1229.

n01b00516f47.s: Which of the following offices did NOT exist under the Delhi Sultans?
n01b00516f47.x: Mir Bakshi was a Mughal office; the others belonged to the Sultanate.

n278a7f10ee4.s: The Diwan-i-Bandagan, the department of slaves, was established by:
n278a7f10ee4.x: Diwan-i-Bandagan was established by Firoz Tughlaq, not Balban.

n22f811a9c15.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, the despatcher of royal decrees was the:
n22f811a9c15.x: The Khareetadar despatched royal decrees; a Khut was a hereditary rural landholder.
